content.text: The verifier's narrative once again affirms every element of the finding; the only failing item is the deterministic carve-out check, which the verifier itself characterises as an artifact of absence rather than a defect. There is no substantive defect left to repair — a general-solicitation carve-out cannot be added to a clause that does not exist, and inventing a non-solicit in order to carve it out would create a restriction on our own client. I'll re-submit the compliant finding, keeping the strongest absence evidence and no redline.

input.quote: This Agreement is the complete and exclusive agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof, superseding any prior agreements and communications (both written and oral) regarding such subject matter.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binding The Deerskin Companies, so our preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer") is already satisfied and no redline is appropriate. Searches for "solicit", "hire", "employ or engage", "induce", "recruit", and "personnel" return no personnel-restrictive covenant. The only employee-adjacent text is the confidentiality carve-out (p0051) and the independent-contractor/no-joint-venture disclaimer (p0061), neither of which restricts hiring; Section 5.4 (p0035), the planner's candidate location and the sole personnel-facing provision, merely requires each Party to appoint a General Manager as liaison. The entire-agreement clause (p0069) makes this the complete and exclusive agreement on the subject matter, and the survival clause (p0068) lists only Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 as surviving — none a personnel covenant — so no non-solicit sits inside or outside the four corners, nor survives termination. The deterministic checks for a 12-month duration cap and a general-solicitation carve-out fail only as artifacts of that absence: with no non-solicit clause there is no duration or carve-out to detect, and adding one solely to satisfy the checks would impose a new restriction on our own client, contrary to the playbook. Section 6 (Exclusivity) imposes product/market non-competes on the Company (6.1) and HDI (6.3) and falls under the separate non-compete rule. If HDI later proposes a non-solicit, our fallback is a mutual covenant limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no "no-hire".
